title: Mitigate telemetry-triggered GC causing tokens/sec collapse on Private clusters
creator: Anika Desai
description:
Summary: Multiple Private customers reported sudden tokens/sec collapse and increased end-to-end latency for mid-length requests (200-700 tokens). The pattern shows healthy throughput then an abrupt drop coincident with a telemetry aggregation spike. Root cause (preliminary): the telemetry aggregator sidecar triggers periodic full-heap scans on the runtime process which increases GC pauses and temporarily fragments the allocator, causing aggressive KV cache eviction and a sustained reduction in effective tokens/sec while the cache warms up. Affected models: long-context decoder-only and chat models using large KV footprint (>= 16GB).

Timeline: 
- 2026-03-09 09:12 UTC: First escalation from "OakFinance" private cluster (region: eu-west-1) — degradation observed during 09:00–09:05 window.
- 2026-03-09 09:26 UTC: Platform metrics show a telemetry flush spike + 120–300ms GC pauses on the runtime process. Tokens/sec drops ~60% for ~3–6 minutes.
- 2026-03-09 10:00 UTC: Confirmed similar signal on a Dedicated cluster and on a customer air-gapped Private eval cluster.
- 2026-03-10 03:15 UTC: Triage call — assigned ENG-78456; immediate hotfix proposed.

Reproduction steps: 
1) Deploy a Private runtime with telemetry aggregation enabled (sidecar config: telemetry.flush_interval=60s) and a model with large KV cache usage.
2) Load sustained traffic (10–20 concurrent streams of 400-token sequences) until a telemetry flush occurs.
3) Observe runtime /prometheus metrics: runtime_gc_pause_ms, kv_cache_evictions, tokens_per_second, allocator_free_frag_ratio.

Root cause analysis (technical): 
- Telemetry aggregator performs synchronous serialization during flush, which pins a thread in the runtime and causes the Go runtime to perform a full mark-sweep (we observed heap growth + full GC traces).
- The runtime allocator becomes fragmented during the pause; KV cache eviction heuristics interpret the transient memory pressure as sustained and evict large prefixes aggressively. Subsequent requests rebuild KV entries slowly which depresses tokens/sec.
- This is particularly visible on Private clusters where the telemetry sidecar and runtime share memory and the instance size for trusted customers was right at the margin.

Immediate mitigations (live hotfix path): 
- Rolling patch for Private images: change telemetry sidecar to use async flush with backpressure (non-blocking serialization) and lower memory working set by streaming instead of buffering. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1592
- Short-term config change: disable full-heap telemetry snapshots by default in Private 1.20 images (runtime flag: --telemetry-snapshot=false) and set kv_cache.eviction_sensitivity=low for targeted clusters.
- Canary rollout: push patched sidecar to 3 customer clusters (OakFinance, BetaRetail, Internal-eval) during low traffic window 2026-03-11 02:00–04:00 UTC.

Longer-term remediation: 
- Update runtime allocator to tolerate short GC-induced fragmentation (reduce eviction aggressiveness when delta memory pressure is transient). Planned work in runtime-allocator epic.
- Replace synchronous telemetry serialization with fully streaming protobuf + bounded worker pool.
- Add a guard in KV eviction: correlate evictions with sustained allocator metrics (e.g., sustained free < threshold for > 30s) before triggering full-prefix eviction.

Monitoring and detection: 
- New Grafana panel added: "Telemetry flush vs GC pause" and an alert: TOKENS_DROP_ON_TELEMETRY (threshold: tokens_per_second drop >= 40% for 120s following telemetry.flush_count increment). Link: https://grafana.internal.redwood/board/telemetry-gc
- Added Prometheus query snippets to runbook: 
  - tokens/sec drop: increase(rate(runtime_tokens_generated[2m])) and compare to 10m baseline.
  - kv_cache_evictions spikes when runtime_gc_pause_ms > 50ms within same minute.

Customer communication: 
- 2026-03-10 05:00 UTC: Notified affected customers (OakFinance, BetaRetail) with initial triage and temporary workaround (disabled telemetry snapshots).
- 2026-03-11 06:00 UTC: Follow-up update after canary showed tokens/sec recovered to baseline.

Rollout plan: 
- Hotfix image push to Private repo (tag: runtime-1.20-hotfix-telemetry-0) and Dedicated pools with selectable config flags.
- Gradual rollout across remaining Private customers over 72 hours with health checks every 30 minutes.
- Post-rollout validation: verify tokens/sec, kv_cache_evictions, and allocator_free_frag_ratio over 24 hours.

Open questions / trade-offs: 
- Disabling rich telemetry reduces trace fidelity for customers who rely on it for debugging. Need to offer per-customer opt-in for full snapshots with SLA caution.
- Making KV eviction less aggressive could raise memory usage in edge cases; require benchmarking on peak-traffic shapes.

Links/Artifacts: 
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1592
- Canary runbook: https://confluence.redwood/d/telemetry-hotfix-canary
- Grafana dashboard (telemetry vs gc): https://grafana.internal.redwood/board/telemetry-gc
- Incident notes (initial): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1TelemetryGCIncident
